property_summary: After calling owned() twice with different senders, the reference contract's owner remains the first caller, while the buggy contract changes owner to the second caller.

After calling owned() once with an initial owner (address(1)), then calling owned() again with address(2) and checking the owner, the reference contract still has owner = address(1) while the buggy contract has owner = address(2).
After deploying C (owner=address(0)), calling owned() from address(1) should revert in reference because msg.sender != owner, whereas buggy contract sets owner=address(1) and succeeds.
After calling owned() from a non-owner address (address(1)), the reference contract reverts, while the buggy contract succeeds and sets owner to address(1).
After deploying C (owner=address(0)), calling owned() from a non-owner address (address(1)): reference reverts, buggy contract succeeds and sets owner to address(1).
After deploying C, calling owned() via a non-owner account (address(1)) succeeds in the buggy version (no revert) but reverts in the correct version due to onlyOwner modifier.
When owner is not set (address(0)), only the buggy version allows a non-owner to call owned() without reverting; the correct version reverts.

When owner is address(this) (the test contract address), a call to owned() from a different prank address (non-owner) reverts on the reference C but succeeds on the buggy M, causing a divergence in whether the call reverts.

When owner is address(this) (the test contract) and a non-owner (address(1)) calls owned(), the reference reverts due to the modifier check, while the buggy version (without the require) does not revert.

When owner is a random user (address(0x123)) and that user calls owned(), the reference passes (no revert) while the buggy version also passes; the divergence must be observed via a different scenario: after owner is transferred to address(0x123), calling owned() from address(0x456) — the reference reverts, the buggy version does not.

After transferring ownership to address(this), calling owned() from a different address (address(1)) reverts on the reference C (due to modifier check) but succeeds on the buggy version (modifier removed).
A non-owner calling owned() reverts on reference but succeeds on buggy version; concrete scenario uses a non-owner address.
